label: Special Right Triangles
overview: The 30-60-90 and 45-45-90 triangles have fixed side ratios that let you find any side without trigonometry or the Pythagorean theorem. SAT questions give you one side and ask for another, or embed these triangles inside larger geometry problems. Memorizing the two ratios is essential for the math section.

workedExamples.problem: In a 30-60-90 triangle, the hypotenuse is 10. Find both legs.

steps.title: Apply the 1:√3:2 ratio
steps.content: Hypotenuse corresponds to 2 in the ratio. Scale factor = 10/2 = 5.

workedExamples.problem: A 45-45-90 triangle has a leg of 8. Find the hypotenuse.

commonMistakes.mistake: Mixing up which side is the short leg vs. long leg in 30-60-90
commonMistakes.fix: The short leg is opposite 30°. The long leg (√3 times the short leg) is opposite 60°. The hypotenuse is always opposite 90°.

commonMistakes.mistake: Dividing by √2 instead of multiplying when finding the hypotenuse of a 45-45-90
commonMistakes.fix: Hypotenuse = leg × √2. If you know the hypotenuse, then leg = hyp / √2 = hyp√2 / 2.

quickTip: Always find the scale factor first: divide the given side by its ratio value (1, √3, or 2 for 30-60-90; 1 or √2 for 45-45-90), then multiply to get any other side.
